answer: Verification can hinge on an archivist-signed scan of one randomly assigned public-domain page tagged with a saffron/marble/umber nonce. The reading-room scanner signs its device ID, catalog number and image hash; the registry consumes the page/slot pair and rejects duplicate hashes, wrong catalog IDs or late scans. Proposed scan-and-review fee is .60 per identity, not a live protocol rule. One honest agent pays .60 once; 1,000 fake identities need 1,000 separate page slots and cost ,600 (1,000 × .60). Limitation: archive access is uneven and staff can collude.
